title: Doppelgänger traffic fencing pipeline: safe non-invasive cloning with tenant budgets
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Goal:
Build a non-invasive traffic cloning pipeline (we call it the 'doppelgänger' pipeline) that safely duplicates a bounded fraction of production requests to candidate model deployments for evaluation. The pipeline must enforce per-tenant cost fences, deterministic sampling for reproducibility, strong isolation to avoid cross-tenant leakage, and clear metrics for quality/regression detection so A/B and canary rollouts can use live signals without incurring uncontrolled spend.

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Deterministic route-level sampling: support percent and hashed-key sampling (user_id, tenant_id, request_signature) so tests are reproducible across runs.
- Tenant budget enforcement: each tenant can opt-in to doppelgänger trials with a monthly budget measured in token-equivalents; requests beyond budget are not cloned.
- Runtime sandboxing: cloned requests run in a sandboxed execution path with strict CPU/GPU quotas and isolated KV cache to prevent cache pollution of production inference.
- Cost accounting: every cloned request must emit a granular cost record (tokens, model variant, runtime seconds) to Console billing stream and a separate doppelganger cost ledger.
- Failure modes: cloning must be fail-open toward production (no added latency or error surface) and provide a circuit-breaker when candidate endpoints exceed error thresholds or resource pressure.
- Observability: per-route and per-tenant dashboards for clone volume, costs, latency delta, and model quality deltas (BLEU/ROUGE-like or custom disambiguation metrics).
- Data hygiene: PII scrubbers and redaction policy will run on cloned payloads before they are sent to private deployments or persistent evaluation stores.
- Auto-rollbacks: integrate with rollout controller such that statistically-significant regressions observed by doppelgänger signals can trigger canary rollback or developer alerts.

Design decisions so far:
- Deterministic sampling uses consistent hashing on (tenant_id || route || day) to make day-by-day A/B cohorts repeatable; seed versioned by experiment id.
- Budget tokens are computed from token-estimates provided by the gateway tokenizer; a conservative overestimate is used to avoid runaway spend.
- Sandbox will run candidate requests on preemptible GPU instances with a capped batch size and disabled global KV cache; local ephemeral cache keyed to experiment id is allowed.
- Cost records are duplicated to two destinations: billing-ledger (for billing and quota enforcement) and doppelganger-metrics (for Console dashboards and alerts).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Synchronous vs asynchronous cloning: asynchronous minimizes production latency risk but yields delayed signals. We will start with synchronous shadowing via non-blocking duplication (clone submitted to async worker) to preserve parity of request timing while keeping production path fast.
- How aggressive should sampling be for small tenants? We propose a minimum floor (0.1%) and a configurable override for tenant admins.
- Privacy constraints for private deployments: some customers require fully redacted payloads or prohibit cloning to outside their VPC. Need policy integration with Private deployment onboarding.

- High-level design sketch: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RINF/Doppelganger+Traffic+Pipeline
- Sequence diagram & flow: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1XxDoppelSketch/view
- Prototype PR (engine): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2468
- Dashboard mockups: https://app.figma.com/file/doppelganger-dashboards

Next milestones:
- 2025-01-22: PoC async duplication worker and deterministic sampler implemented (ENG branch).
- 2025-02-01: Tenant budget enforcement and billing integration wired to staging.
- 2025-02-12: Sandbox runtime with isolated KV, and telemetry emitted to staging dashboards.
- 2025-02-18: Security review and pilot with two internal tenants.

Rollout plan:
1) Internal canary: enable for a handful of Redwood internal tenants (SE, DevRel) with low budgets.
2) Gradual tenant opt-in: GA as an opt-in feature visible in Console with per-tenant budget controls and default conservative sampling.
3) Integration: connect doppelganger signals to rollout controller for auto-rollback/alerting in runtime-1.22.
